st: Between Giorgia Meloni, the economics Nobel and the modern individual

sec.t: ff.77.1 Is the “traditional family” a thing of the past?
sec.p: OK, we've talked about the crisis of the “boomer” value system:

Hand me those Meloni (melons). Giorgia Meloni claims the demographic crisis is tied to the collapse of traditional family values. Yet a study using a European survey on family values (EVS) tried to check whether this correlation with fertility rates actually exists. It found…
Pope Francis argues it's more of an economic issue. But with what I spend on Michelin-starred dinners, trips to the other side of the world and Ironman entries, I could probably support a child.
Does the career woman have no time for kids? It's not an easy question, so much so that this year it earned Harvard's Claudia Goldin the Nobel Prize in Economics.
So where's the answer? Maybe we're simply more individualistic?
